question.leadin: This man was born near Lake Baikal with the name Temujin ("TEH-moo-jin").
question.text: Name this man who was proclaimed "universal ruler" in a 1206 assembly.
question.clue: The creator of the Yassa Code, he declined to name his son Jochi as successor, and his general Subotai led the conquest of the Khwarezmian Empire.

swap.text: Famous Tang poet Li Bai was born in a town along this trading route from China to the Mediterranean. A particular Chinese fabric gave this trading route its name.
swap.clue: A 2015 best-selling history book by Peter Frankopan is titled for the plural form of this entity.

question.leadin: This ruler defeated Tokhtamysh [TOKE-TAM-ISH] at the Battle of the Terek River. --.
question.text: Name this conqueror from Samarkand who sacked Damascus and Delhi.
question.clue: This man's grandson, the ruler and astronomer Ulugh Beg is buried in the same mausoleum, the Gur-e Amir.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about the foreign policy of George W. Bush.
swap.text: Following the 9/11 attacks, the United States invaded Afghanistan in order to overthrow this political group which controlled the country and harbored Al Qaeda.
swap.clue: It was opposed by a contingent of non-Pashtun warlords known as the Northern Alliance.

question.text: The An Lushan Rebellion forced the Tang to retreat from its Western Protectorate, which would later be conquered by an empire named for this region governed from Lhasa.
question.clue: Songtsan Gampo founded an empire in this region, later home to a line of religious leaders begun by Gendun Drup.

swap.leadin: A political cartoon depicting this period shows Emir Sher Ali asking the reader to "save him from [his] friends"
swap.text: Name this Anglo-Russian conflict in the mid-1800s over Central Asia, which included the partitioning of Persia into spheres of influence, the Eastern Question, and the Anglo-Afghan wars.
swap.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people messing with calendars.
question.text: As president of this country, Sarparmurat Niyazov renamed April "Gurbansoltan"after his mother. Even more hilariously, bread was also renamed Gurbansoltan during Niyazov's rule in this country.
question.clue: The Rukhnama, or "Book of Soul," was a propaganda work written by a former head of this state, Saparmurat Niyazov.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the tribe known as the Alans, who migrated to Europe in the late 4th and early 5th centuries.
swap.text: In the late 9th century, the Alans established an independent kingdom in this mountain range. A nation in this range is often recognized as the first to establish Christianity as its official religion, doing so in 301 A.D.
swap.clue: Gold and silver tubes, possibly used to drink beer, that were found in this region were made by the Maykop culture, which, like this region's Kura-Araxes culture, constructed burial mounds called kurgans.

question.leadin: In 1839, the British deposed the king of this territory and replaced him with a puppet ruler.
question.text: Identify this modern-day country that ceded territory via the Treaty of Gandamak to British. Britain initially got involved in this country after an attack on its city of Herat.
question.clue: Gubdullin Hekmatyar fought in a conflict in this country that resulted in the formation of the Seven Party alliance.

swap.leadin: Answer the following relating to nuclear weapons treaties.
swap.text: The United States refused to ratify the SALT II treaty after the Soviet Union invaded this country in 1979. The CIA provided arms to the Mujahedeen to help them repel the Soviets from this country.
swap.clue: One invasion of this country was ended by the Treaty of Gandamak and took place during the "Great Game."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of a mountainous nation that's been in the news a lot.
question.text: In 1893, the British set up this border between Afghanistan and Pakistan based on geographical features, not ethnic regions. This idiotic idea continues to lend itself today to ethnic tensions.
question.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

swap.text: In 2015, holographic projections replaced these two statues in a namesake valley in central Afghanistan, after they were destroyed by the Taliban in an act of cultural destruction.
swap.answerHtml: Bamiyan Buddhas [or Buddhas of Bamiyan; prompt on partial answers]
swap.clue: This World Heritage site in Afghanistan consists of notable religious representations. It was partially destroyed in 2001.

question.text: Rulers of Rouran used this title that was later adopted by Bumin and the Gokturks. In the 13th century, this title was adopted by Temujin.
question.answerHtml: khan [or khagan; accept Genghis Khan or Chinggis Khan; prompt on emperor]
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: A vizier of an empire whose capital was this city may have been a secret Manichaean.
swap.text: Name this city, the capital of the Samanid Empire whose rulers commissioned Ferdowsi to write the Shahnameh. Alongside the Khanate of Khiva, an emirate ruled from this city later became a Russian protectorate.
swap.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

question.text: This so-called "Stalin of Mongolia" sought to reunite Outer and Inner Mongolia, but was thwarted by the real Stalin. He served as leader of Mongolia from 1939 to 1952.
question.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

swap.text: The Afghan side at Panipat was led by this ruler, who had previously invaded India as a general of Nader Shah. This ruler united the Pashtun tribes to form the first modern Afghan state under the Durrani dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Ahmad Shah Durrani [accept Ahmad Shah Abdali; prompt on Shah Durrani or Shah Abdali alone]
swap.clue: This cavalry commander discovered the leader of the Afsharid kingdom assassinated in a tent, prompting him to abscond with the royal seal and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

question.leadin: The shadowy figure Rysbek Akmatbayev used this event to gain a significant hold over his country's parliament, the Jogorku Kenesh.
question.text: Name this event, which began with PMK-coordinated protests in cities like Jalal-Abad and Osh. This 2005 revolution ousted Askar Akayev.
question.answerHtml: Tulip Revolution (The Tulip Revolution took place in Kyrgyzstan.)
question.clue: Roza Otunbayeva, an atheist, became Kyrgyzstan's first female president in 2010, five years after she participated in this revolution, which overthrew Askar Akayev's presidency and replaced him with Kurmanbek Bakiyev.

swap.text: Supposedly, Janibeg of the Golden Horde used trebuchets to hurl corpses at the besieged defenders of this Crimean city, leading to the spread of the Black Plague into Europe.
swap.clue: This city which was besieged by the Golden Horde in the 1340s. Gabriel de Mussis claims that Jani Beg catapulted corpses over the walls of this city in an early act of biological warfare.

question.leadin: They conquered their namesake city after Alp Tigin was dismissed from office and used his slaves to take it over.
question.text: Identify this Islamic dynasty based out of Afghanistan that brought Islam to the heart of India under their greatest ruler Mahmud.
question.clue: One of the dynasties that sprung up in Transoxiana after the demise of the Abbasids was this one, whose founder Sabuktigin founded it by seizing Samanid territory. Its sultan Mahmud patronized the poet Ferdowsi.

swap.text: This "dog of war," along with Batu Khan, devastated Hungarian forces at the Battle of Mohi as the master strategist of the Mongol army under Genghis Khan and Ogedei Khan.
swap.clue: This general was listed as one of the "four dogs of Temujin."
